purpose: Test the smallest covariant one-metric geometry-only action that can produce the successful galaxy low-acceleration limit without invisible matter.
physical_postulates: Baryonic stress-energy is the only material source.
Matter and light couple minimally to one physical metric g_ab.
The independent connection is flat and torsion-free; it contributes no freely specifiable halo source.
The Sigma response is a nonlinear gravitational self-interaction of the STEGR nonmetricity scalar, not a material fluid.
The high-nonmetricity limit is the symmetric-teleparallel equivalent of GR.
All isolated systems use the same asymptotic boundary rule and the same acceleration scale.
No galaxy or cluster label, per-object force constant, or lensing-only multiplier is allowed.

action.nonmetricity_tensor: Q_a_mn=nabla_a g_mn with flat torsion-free Gamma

decision_rule: Advance only if the covariant action has a regular non-GR lensing response and passes both the galaxy and raw cluster gates. If its regular weak-field branch is exactly no-slip AQUAL, inherit the already-spent AQUAL scores and retire this action as a unifier without parameter fitting.
claim_boundary: The action family f(Q) and symmetric-teleparallel gravity are prior art.
This cycle tests whether the specific GR-to-standard-mu geometric interpolation supplies the missing cluster response.
A weak-field no-go does not reject every nonmetricity theory; it rejects the one-invariant regular isolated branch tested here.
